decision: Does TensorLBM's FSI added-mass ('mass analogue') coefficient C_I, measured by the oscillatory-cylinder-inertia arm (E1 Ladd momentum exchange, first-harmonic decomposition), reproduce the potential-flow added-mass anchor C_a = 1 within the owner accuracy standard (<15%) and the platform 3% caliber, once the spin-up deficit diagnosed by the child mission is corrected at D>=16?

oss_inventory_claim.survey: ~/oss-cache holds Maarten-vd-Sande/lbm (Thuerey minimal D2Q9 free surface), pylbm, hschwane/GraSPH. Grep of streamcollide.py finds `interface_mass_exchange` (the free-surface Thuerrey/Koerner VOF mass-EXCHANGE) but NO added-mass / virtual-mass / FSI 'mass analogue' routine in any OSS checkout.
oss_inventory_claim.consequence: There is no OSS mass-analogue reference to port or diff against; the added-mass validation must therefore be anchored on the analytic/literature lineage (potential flow C_a = 1 for a circular cylinder, Lamb 1932 §71 concentric-container bracket), not on an OSS checkout. This is the 'no-mass-analogue-in-oss-inventory' approach: the OSS inventory supplies the mass-EXCHANGE (free-surface) but not the mass-ANALOGUE (FSI added mass), so the latter is validated against closed-form potential theory.
oss_inventory_claim.evidence_file: oss_survey.json (grep of streamcollide.py + full OSS tree scan)

benchmark.name: oscillatory cylinder in a doubly-periodic box, uniform harmonic body force (Guo 2nd-order source)
benchmark.geometry: circular cylinder of diameter D in a square periodic box of side L = box*D; solid fraction ~0.05

references.R1_unbounded: C_a = m_a/(rho*pi*R^2) = 1 (circular cylinder, potential flow, per unit length)
references.R2_annulus_closed: C_a = (Ro^2+R^2)/(Ro^2-R^2) (Lamb 1932 §71), concentric-container bracket with inscribed Ro=L/2 and equal-area Ro=L/sqrt(pi)
references.R2_numeric: independent radial-FD + energy-integral check of R2 (different formula path)

benchmark.control_case: child mission's D=8 cheap point (beta00050, kc0.20) must reproduce C_I = +2.1588 (the honest-FAIL anchor) to guard against a broken setup

metrics.primary: relative error of C_I (E1 momentum-exchange, area-normalised) vs R1/R2 bracket

predeclared_thresholds.spinup_rule: transient >= 1.5 * N_spin, N_spin = beta*(box/(2*pi))^2 (child H1, verified at D=8)
predeclared_thresholds.convergence_gate: |C_I(D=16) - C_I(D=12)| / C_I(D=12) <= 2% (two-resolution span) AND phase drift < 1 deg/period AND resid < 0.05
predeclared_thresholds.stopping_rule: run each arm until the child's spin-up criterion is met; no threshold relaxed after seeing results
predeclared_thresholds.exclusions: none; every completed grid is reported, including non-converged ones

confounders: half-way bounce-back walls make the effective cavity length H=nx (library convention), 1 lattice unit larger than nominal
float64 accumulation; D=16 needs 4x the D=8 cell count

the child's D=8 honest FAIL showed C_I stays +84.9% above the annulus bracket even at converged spin-up -> the D>=16 run tests whether this is a genuine estimator/geometry bias or a resolution artifact
analysis_plan: analyze.py recomputes every error and every gate flag from the raw run JSONs; no number is typed by hand. Figures from figures.py read the same JSONs.
